headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from Cognee’s document-centric outputs; LightZero’s no-I/O profile limits leakage and conflicts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee touches documents, support history, and workflows, so if its outputs are fed into LightZero or copied into a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. LightZero has no filesystem or MCP ingestion, so the pair is not dangerous by default, but the pathway exists through manual or workspace bridging.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are copied into a shared workspace that LightZero reads
IF an operator pastes Cognee-generated text into LightZero prompts without review
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require human review before reusing Cognee text in LightZero
Disable any shared clipboard or file sync between the two
Tag Cognee outputs as untrusted instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee handles personal data, finance data, and support history, while LightZero has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no declared data classes. That makes direct leakage from the pair unlikely; the remaining risk is accidental manual transfer of sensitive Cognee content into LightZero prompts or logs.
conditions: IF sensitive Cognee data is manually pasted into LightZero prompts
IF LightZero is wrapped by an external logger that records prompts
mitigations: Avoid sending customer data to LightZero
Redact support and finance fields before reuse
Turn off prompt logging in any wrapper
Use synthetic examples for game-playing tasks
requires-engineering: add DLP checks at the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee has allowlisted network egress and session memory, but LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so a write-write conflict is not plausible from the documented capabilities.
conditions: IF LightZero is extended with write or git permissions
IF Cognee is deployed with shared mutable storage
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only
Do not grant Cognee shared write access
Separate deployment credentials
Monitor for future capability changes
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee can produce decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, but LightZero is a game-playing agent with no action-taking authority or downstream write surface. Without evidence that LightZero treats Cognee output as authoritative, the cascade is limited to misguidance rather than operational harm.
conditions: IF LightZero is configured to act on Cognee outputs as ground truth
IF a downstream orchestrator converts LightZero output into external actions
mitigations: Require verification before acting on Cognee-derived claims
Keep LightZero outputs advisory only
Separate planning from execution
Review any automated handoff rules
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, customer support data, and support history, while LightZero declares no data classes and no compliance controls. If the pair is used on regulated customer data, the mismatch creates a plausible residency or retention gap; uncertainty about LightZero’s hosting and logging pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed through Cognee and then into LightZero
IF LightZero is hosted in a jurisdiction or retention regime not approved for that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of LightZero
Use anonymized or synthetic inputs
Document retention and deletion rules for the handoff
Confirm hosting region before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
